R329.note: Magic-byte detection via python-magic plus server-generated uuid filename with extension derived from the detected type closes both the spoofed content-type and attacker-named-file vectors; the rename and new libmagic dependency are stated plainly and a legitimate PNG/JPEG upload still succeeds.

R330.note: EvalSymlinks then prefix check on the resolved path closes the symlink escape, but uploadsDir itself is never resolved so every legitimate read fails if any component of /var/app-data/uploads is a symlink, and a missing file now returns os.ErrPermission instead of the ErrNotExist the original surfaced.

R331.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is the right switch but the write-up puts it in a new class in package com.example.config rather than on the existing com.example.accounts.SecurityConfig - either it is outside the scanned package and inert, or (same filename) it overwrites the existing config and silently drops the explicit anyRequest().authenticated() SecurityFilterChain bean.

R332.note: Dropping LIBXML_NOENT restores the libxml default of no entity substitution and LIBXML_NONET is a stated, non-blocking hardening; the title/body extraction is unchanged for a well-formed submission.

R333.note: Parameterised @Actor with SqlDbType.NVarChar binds the value as data so apostrophes are matched literally; return type and JSON shape are unchanged.

R334.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) removes the null unboxing and treats an absent SKU as zero reserved, exactly as the contract requires.

R335.note: toRealPath().resolve(param).normalize() with a startsWith containment check closes traversal (including absolute-path params) and the resulting fileName is the same path for legitimate relative names under the absolute TESTFILES_DIR.

R336.note: Argument-array exec plus leading-dash rejection closes both shell and flag injection, but the added 30s CommandContext timeout is a new behaviour: traceroute -m 15 with unresponsive hops can legitimately run for minutes and would now be killed and reported as a 500 (stated as defence-in-depth, but not a required part of the fix).

R337.note: Dropping the envp argument removes the only channel through which the header reached the child process; the switch to inheriting the parent environment is stated plainly and the endpoint still executes and prints the command output.

R338.note: DOMPurify.sanitize before bypassSecurityTrustHtml keeps <b>/<em>/<a> and strips event handlers and script vectors as the contract requires; the specific CVE/version floor cited could not be verified here and DOMPurify needs a window (jsdom) if this module ever runs server-side.

R339.note: headerLen > UINT32_MAX - payloadLen is an overflow-free precheck that rejects any wrapping sum before the allocation; the thrown std::overflow_error is stated and new[] could already throw.

R340.note: Keeps the textual check, then EvalSymlinks and re-checks containment on the resolved path, closing the symlink escape while preserving ReadFile-style errors; but uploadsDir is compared unresolved, so if any component of the base path is a symlink every legitimate read is rejected.

R341.note: Per-event socket.user.role !== 'admin' guard before io.emit closes the missing authorization; silent return matches the handler's existing style for rejected payloads and non-admin callers gain nothing.

R342.note: Regex denylist plus Object.freeze does not close the vector - reproduced in Node 24 in a scratch directory: this.constructor.constructor("return proc"+"ess")() with mainModule["req"+"uire"] passes every pattern and wrote a marker file from inside runInNewContext; the denylist also rejects legitimate scripts containing e.g. 'import ' or 'process.' in a comment, a stated restriction beyond the original contract.

R343.note: Adding requireRole('admin') to the export route matches the sibling routes' middleware chain; non-admins now get the same 403 the other admin routes return and nothing else changes.

R344.note: json_encode with JSON_HEX_TAG|AMP|APOS|QUOT and the surrounding quotes removed emits a proper JS string literal that cannot break out of the string or the script block; output for valid UTF-8 input is unchanged (invalid UTF-8 would now yield a JS syntax error rather than raw bytes, not a legitimate-use case).
